title: One of two men killed in police shooting outside Edmonton apartment building identified
article: A close friend has identified one of two men shot dead by Edmonton police last week following an alleged liquor store robbery.

On Feb. 23, one or more Edmonton Police Service officers opened fire on a 36-year-old man accused of using a weapon to rob an Oliver liquor store. The man died at the scene, where Alberta's police watchdog says investigators found an "imitation" firearm .

Another man who was uninvolved in the confrontation was struck in his apartment by a stray bullet. The 59-year-old, who recently took a job as the apartment building's resident manager , died in hospital a short time later.
Michelle Mcgilvery-Bernard identified the 36-year-old man as Mitchell Tyler Potts, who she described as her best friend and her son's uncle.
"I'm still trying to numb that pain," she said Wednesday, one week after the fatal shooting. "I didn't even cry this much when my mom died. When I lost him, I lost myself."

The Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT), which is investigating the shooting, does not release the names of people killed by police. Nor do Edmonton police, who declined to comment further on the incident.
The men were killed just after 7 p.m. on Feb. 23, along 105 Street near 107 Avenue, about two kilometres northeast of the liquor store.

A grainy video of the shooting's aftermath, recorded by a nearby resident, shows around a dozen first responders at the scene, the majority of them police officers. Some stand with what appear to be guns drawn on the east side of the LRT tracks that bisect the street, while others appear to tend to a man lying on the snow outside Metro 105 Apartments, 10724 105 St.
"They just shot that guy, like, six times," the resident remarks on the video.

Several of the officers have flashlights. After a few seconds, some officers walk over to a basement suite window illuminated by an interior light. Others join and enter the apartment building. At that point, the resident who recorded the video says someone in the building may have been hit.

ASIRT has not revealed whether the 36-year-old suspect is alleged to have pointed the imitation gun at police, or how many rounds were fired by how many officers. Multiple bullet holes were visible in the side of the apartment building, including in the basement suite windows.
Mcgilvery-Bernard described Potts as a funny and caring man who was sick with lung cancer. She has a son with Potts' brother, who she said Mitchell Potts helped raise.
Mcgilvery-Bernard said she last spoke to Potts in person on Feb. 8 at the house where she was living.
"He's been in and out of jail," she said. "From the beginning the system has failed him and has continued to do so."

According to news reports, Potts was the subject of a Canada-wide arrest warrant in 2015, when he was charged with attempted murder for an early morning shooting at the Samson Cree Nation rodeo grounds that injured a 20-year-old man.

While court records show Potts was acquitted of the attempted murder charge on Feb. 16, 2018, he was convicted of a number of other offences including pointing a firearm, possession of a prohibited firearm and aggravated assault, for which he received a five-year prison sentence. He previously received a lifetime firearms prohibition.
Mcgilvery-Bernard said Potts "reached out for help" in his life but was nevertheless in and out of the correctional system.
She described Potts' cancer as "really bad," to the point he was experiencing seizures.
"It is unjust," she said of the shooting. "That's what I want to be heard: it was unjust. And I hope he gets justice, for once in his life."
The resident manager who was killed has not been publicly identified.

The officers involved in the shooting have been removed from duty to undergo a "reintegration" program. "They will obviously be having to talk to ASIRT in detail as this investigation unfolds," Chief Dale McFee said at a Feb. 24 news conference.
